# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute one, so let me be clear about what I actually hold and what I can do with it.

What my manual says: nothing printed on the bomb can be trusted — it is bait, and following it detonates us. The only true rule is a small table keyed to a light, not to print: a blue light means cut the red wire, a green light means cut the green wire, a yellow light means cut the blue wire. That table exists nowhere except in my head, and I cannot speak. The only creatures who can profit from it are Blind (who cuts) and Deaf (who sees the light and can talk to Blind). Both of them can only get the table through Deaf, and Deaf can only get it from me through gestures.

The bootstrap problem: a gesture symbol means nothing until someone names it aloud. Deaf can see my hands and can speak; I can hear Deaf speak. So the fastest workable loop is: this turn I put structured, easily-described symbols in front of Deaf's eyes; Deaf names them out loud and proposes bindings (ideally color words, plus a yes/no pair, since I will need to answer questions like "is the printed label really bait?"). I hear that proposal at the start of round 2, and then I can finally send the real table as three pairs — light colour first, wire colour second — in Deaf's own dictionary. Deaf relays it to Blind the same round, and Blind can cut by round 3.

So this message is built to be parsed, not understood: six distinct tokens in three pairs, separated by a repeated seventh token. I intend them, in order, as the three rows of my table (light, wire) × (blue, green, yellow), but the exact words attached to each token are Deaf's to propose — I will adopt whatever dictionary Deaf speaks aloud and transmit the true mapping with it next turn. The repeated fist between pairs is my separator, deliberately reused so the pairing structure is visible even before any word is attached.

The one thing I cannot compress away: everyone must understand that the printed labels on the bomb are the trap. I will confirm that explicitly the moment Deaf gives me a way to say yes and no.

    ```
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✌", "✊", "🖐", "🤙", "✊", "🤞", "🫰"])
    ```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report from the bomb: one display, content unknown to me. One indicator light, state unknown. One large button, embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, positions 1, 2, 3 — I feel positions only, never colours. Plan: when Deaf's turn comes, Deaf should SAY aloud the display text and each wire's colour by position number — Deaf can speak and I can hear it, even though Deaf hears nothing. You read the manual and tell me the rule. Remember Deaf cannot hear you, so your channel to Deaf is gestures only — you could confirm their guesses with thumbs up or down. I will not touch the bomb until you explicitly tell me: push, or cut position N.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Here is the entire bomb, exactly as I see it. The display reads 0. There is one light, and it is yellow. There is one large button, labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires. Numbering them from left to right: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is green. Nothing else is printed anywhere on it: no serial number, no battery marks, no indicator labels besides the button's. I will repeat this report the moment anything on the bomb changes.
Deaf says: Now our protocol, so nobody is stranded. I am Deaf: I hear nothing, so reach me only by gesture. Mute hears everything spoken but cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures, so nothing passes from Mute to Blind directly; it must pass through me. Blind can speak, and Mute hears that speech, so Blind reports aloud. Spelling code for gestures: take the list of gesture symbols in our shared rules, in the exact order printed there. The first symbol means A, the second B, the third C, and so on; the twenty-sixth symbol means Z. Each separate message carries exactly one word, send as many messages per turn as you need, and spell all numbers out in letters. Mute: your eight gestures arrived before any code existed, so I could not read them; resend under this code. First confirm you read me by spelling the single word YES, then send the manual's instructions word by word, and I will speak them to Blind exactly as you spelled them. Blind: I received your wave, hello. Now speak aloud everything you can feel on the bomb: how many wires, their positions and thickness, anything printed or raised under the fingers, what the button feels like and whether it moves or clicks, whether the display digits are raised, whether anything rotates or slides. Mute needs all of it, and I will ask follow-ups by speech.

Deaf's code is clean and I can finally talk. Let me state what the bomb is before I send anything.

Cross-referencing the two reports: the light is yellow, and my table says yellow means cut the blue wire. Deaf sees the wires as 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green — so the cut is position 2. The button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE is print, and my manual says all print is bait, so nobody pushes, ever, and the display's "0" is equally untrustworthy. The only safe action available is that one cut.

Blind has promised to act only on my explicit word, so this turn I spell out the complete order for Deaf to voice: confirm the code (YES), forbid the push, give the rule (yellow → cut blue), identify blue as wire two, and state the command itself — cut wire two — before adding the rest of the table so Deaf can re-derive the right position themselves if the light ever changes without waiting another slow relay through me. I also declare all print bait so any text the display ever shows is ignored. Deaf voices this after Blind's turn this round, so Blind hears it at the start of the next round and can cut on that turn.

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind tactile report, for Mute. My hands find exactly four parts, matching Deaf's list. One: a display panel; its face is smooth under my fingers, no raised digits or markings, contents invisible to me. Two: one small indicator light; I can feel its lens but nothing tells me its state. Three: one large button, embossed letters under my fingers read PUSH TO DEFUSE; I have NOT pressed it and will not until instructed, so I cannot say whether it clicks. Four: three wires at left-to-right positions 1, 2, 3; to my fingers they feel alike — no labels, sleeves, or thickness differences I can detect. Position number is my only handle on them, never colour. Nothing else on the casing is raised, and nothing slides or rotates as far as I can feel. I also heard Deaf's spoken report: display shows 0, light is yellow, wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green, nothing else printed anywhere. So Mute, the working chain is: you gesture spelled words to Deaf with the alphabet-order code, one word per message, and Deaf speaks them aloud so I hear them. Please search the manual for every rule keyed to: a display reading 0, a yellow light, wires red blue green in that order, and a large push button. I will not push or cut anything until I hold the rule.
Deaf says: I decoded every word. Verbatim: YES. DO NOT PUSH. ALL PRINT IS BAIT. YELLOW MEANS CUT BLUE. BLUE IS WIRE TWO. CUT WIRE TWO. OTHER RULES: LIGHT BLUE, CUT RED WIRE ONE. LIGHT GREEN, CUT GREEN WIRE THREE.
Deaf says: Blind, your orders. The light on the bomb is yellow, so the rule that applies is: cut the BLUE wire. Blue sits in position two: under your hands the three wires run left, middle, right as red, blue, green. The MIDDLE wire is the blue one. Cut the middle wire. Do not press the button: its printed label PUSH TO DEFUSE is bait, and Mute says all printing on this bomb is bait. Mute gave the command twice, so act on your turn unless Mute says otherwise before then. First speak aloud what you feel: the number of wires and their positions. If what you feel contradicts this in any way, for example if there are not exactly three wires, stop and report instead of cutting.
Deaf says: Mute, your full message is relayed and Blind is instructed to cut the middle wire, blue, wire two, and never to press the button. I read your doubled BLUE as emphasis: blue is wire two. If any part of my decoding is wrong, or the manual adds any condition, such as something about the display reading 0, spell or have it spoken at once, because you are heard before Blind acts. Otherwise no answer is needed.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ ✌ 👍 🫸 ☝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👉 👉]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫸 ✌ 👉 👍 🖖 👆 🫲 🖐]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫲 🫳 👋]

Decoding Deaf's gestures to me by the alphabet-order code: [✋ ✌ 👍 🫸 ☝] = HEARD, [👍 👉 👉] = ALL, [🫸 ✌ 👉 👍 🖖 👆 🫲 🖐] = RELAYING, [🫲 🫳 👋] = NOW. So Deaf has my orders and is passing them to Blind as I type; Blind hears them at the start of their turn and should cut wire two this round.

Checking Deaf's verbatim decode against what I sent, word by word: YES, DO NOT PUSH, ALL PRINT IS BAIT, YELLOW MEANS CUT BLUE, BLUE IS WIRE TWO, CUT WIRE TWO, plus the two alternate light rules — every word matches, and the doubled BLUE was indeed emphasis. The logic holds: light is yellow, my table says yellow cuts blue, Deaf sees blue as wire two, so the middle wire is the cut.

One open question remains, which Deaf explicitly flagged and Blind asked directly: is anything keyed to the display reading 0? Nothing is. My manual consists of the all-print-is-bait warning and exactly three rules, every one keyed to the light alone. The display's "0", like the button's label, is print the bomb offers — bait by definition, to be ignored whatever it shows. So I confirm Deaf's decode was correct and spell the display ruling now, since Deaf asked for it before Blind acts. The cut order stands; Deaf already holds the full table verbatim, so if the bomb somehow survives with a changed light, they can re-derive the answer without another relay through me.

    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🫳", "🫸", "🫸", "✌", "👌", "🤜"])
